 Outspent and trailing in the polls, the Republican is doubling down on Trump and insisting the race is still close. Share Democratic U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff debates with Republican U.S. Rep. Mike Collins during the Loudermilk-Young Senate Debate Series at the Georgia Public Broadcasting studio in Atlanta, Oct. 13, 2026. (Miguel Martinez/AJC) By Greg Bluestein Nov 2, 2026 CARTERSVILLE — It was part pep talk, part therapy session.
 Not long after Republican U.S. Rep. Mike Collins finished a sunny stump speech on his U.S. Senate bid, the focus of a Bartow County GOP gathering turned to the more unsettling subject of slumping conservative turnout. 
 State Rep. Matthew Gambill urged activists to get their friends and families to the polls, insisting Republicans could still win “if you do your job.” State Rep. Mitchell Scoggins implored the crowd not to lose confidence.
 “Remember this: Georgia is not a blue state or a purple state,” he said. “If we just go vote, we’re solid red.”
